title: Proposal for Legislation to Deal with Foreign Interference of Singapore’s Election and Politics
what_it_is: Proposal for Legislation to Deal with Foreign Interference of Singapore’s Election and Politics

sections.label: Foreign interference in elections
sections.summary: A question asks what Singapore can learn from foreign interference in other countries' elections and politics, and whether new laws are needed.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui
sentences.text: asked the Prime Minister (a) what can Singapore learn from the various incidences of foreign interferences in the elections and politics of countries, such as the US, Australia, France and Germany; and (b) whether there is a need to introduce new laws or further strengthen existing laws to deal with foreign interference and Singaporeans who work with foreign actors to influence Singapore's elections and politics.

sections.label: US Facebook users exposed
sections.summary: Over two years, about 126 million US Facebook users were exposed to content generated by a foreign operation.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: Over two years, about 126 million US Facebook users were exposed to content generated by this foreign operation.

sections.label: Foreign-linked social media campaigns
sections.summary: Foreign-linked social media accounts spread anti-immigration falsehoods, pro-Brexit messages and leaked Macron campaign data.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: A steady stream of anti-immigration falsehoods by foreign-linked social media accounts made people feel threatened and built a narrative of a British government that was failing to protect its citizens.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: There is also research suggesting that more than 150,000 foreign-linked accounts tweeted over 45,000 pro-Brexit messages in the last 48 hours of the campaign.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: Just two days before the second round of voting, nine gigabytes of data hacked from presidential candidate Emmanuel Macron’s campaign were leaked online.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: In just three and a half hours, the leak was tweeted 47,000 times, with some suspicious Twitter accounts, likely bots in action, posting more than 150 tweets per hour.

sections.label: Australia's foreign interference laws
sections.summary: Australia's parliament passed a package of laws in June 2018 aimed at preventing foreign interference in their politics.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: Australia’s parliament passed a package of laws in June 2018, aimed at preventing foreign interference in their politics.

sections.label: Updating legal framework
sections.summary: The legal framework must be updated and enhanced to counter hostile information campaigns, with new legislation having two broad objectives.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: Second, we must update and enhance our legal framework, which is outmoded against modern and technologically-sophisticated tactics, 	to counter hostile information campaigns.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: On hostile information campaigns, new legislation should have two broad objectives.

sections.label: Threat real, action later
sections.summary: The threat is real and action on these issues will come later this year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: The threat is real and we will be moving on these issues later this year.

sections.label: Huang Jing foreign agent case
sections.summary: The Government identified Huang Jing, a Lee Kuan Yew School of Public Policy academic, as an agent of influence for a foreign country.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: More recently, Members may recall the case of Huang Jing, a Lee Kuan Yew School of Public Policy academic who the Government identified as an agent of influence, acting on behalf of a foreign country.

sections.label: SingHealth hacking incident
sections.summary: The SingHealth hacking incident was an attempt to extract Singaporeans' health information, with the Prime Minister as the specific target.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Members will also recall the SingHealth hacking incident last year, essentially an attempt to extract health information of Singaporeans, with the Prime Minister being the specific target.

sections.label: Avatar accounts on alternative media
sections.summary: Around 40% of comments on alternative media outlets' social media pages came from avatar accounts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Around 40% of the comments on alternative media outlets' pages on social media came from avatar accounts.

sections.label: Government to consider Report and legislation
sections.summary: The Government will consider the Report and will also consider legislation in both of these areas this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: The Government will consider the Report and will also consider legislation in both of these areas this year.
